newsitem.title: USA: Dole vows Calif. fight, hits Clinton on immigration.
newsitem.headline: Dole vows Calif. fight, hits Clinton on immigration.

text.p: Bob Dole promised on Thursday a get-tough battle for vote-rich California as he charged U.S. President Bill Clinton with a "sorry record" on illegal immigration, a heated issue in this state.

Dole, behind in polls but upbeat after his final debate with Clinton on Wednesday night in San Diego, told reporters he would make an "all out" fight for the nation's most populous state's 54 electoral votes.

And following up on his aggressive attack on Clinton's White House for alleged ethical lapses, the Republican candidate told a partisan audience here in a speech that "We're going to get tough in this campaign, you haven't seen anything yet."
Although polls after the debate in San Diego showed that people by a roughly two-to-one margin thought Clinton won, Dole seemed pumped up by his get-tough performance.
"I'm going to fight for California -- and I will win California on Nov. 5," he said.

Dole's campaign manager, Scott Reed, told reporters that an overnight Dole campaign tracking poll showed him closing to within eight percentage points of Clinton in this state where the president held a lead of over 20 points in polls last month.

Reed said the campaign would commit whatever resources were necessary to win California, the richest prize on election day with its electoral votes representing about one out of every five of the 270 needed to win.
The campaign has been agonizing whether to make an all-out fight for California and spend precious dollars for advertising and travel in a state that Clinton has counted as his own.

Dole coupled his commitment to fight for California by accusing Clinton of being soft on illegal immigrants, which has been a major problem in this state that pays millions of dollars in health and education benefits to immigrants.

"Bill Clinton comes to this state with sympathetic words for the people of California," said Dole. "But the problem is this -- when decision time comes, whenever he has to choose between California taxpayers and the militant groups who demand public support for illegal aliens -- he sides with the special interests."

Dole said it is the federal government's responsibility to protect its borders. "During the last four years, it has failed in that duty -- big time," said Dole. "And you are the ones who pay the price for that monumental failure."
He said "Right alongside the administration's sorry record on illegal immigration is its dismal record on illegal drugs."
California, he said, suffers the consequences of the drug problem. "In four years, interdiction at our borders has dropped dramatically," Dole said.

Dole also reached out to other western states in his speech here. "We are going to end the war on the West, and end the war on California," Dole claimed. "Whether the issue is property rights, conservation policy, regulation, or taxes -- our western states should not be taking orders from faraway potentates on the Potomac."
Talking to reporters before arriving here, Dole pledged to end what he called the "sleaze factor" in the White House if elected president in 19 days.
He also took a shot at Democrats for raising some $140,000 during a fundraiser last April for Vice President Al Gore held in a Buddhist temple, as reported in Thursday's Los Angeles Times.
"Now they are out raising money in Buddhist temples where they take a vow of poverty," Dole told reporters, adding that perhaps Gore next "will have a fundraiser at the homeless shelter."
